title: How Amul's 'Utterly Butterly Delicious' Girl Quietly Became India's Most Iconic Mascot
context: Amul's topical, hand-painted billboards started in 1966 and never paid for distribution — a marketing decision that became one of India's longest-running ad campaigns. The mascot pre-dates television advertising in India.

title: Reliance Jio's Free-Data Gambit: The ₹1.5 Lakh Crore Bet That Re-priced Indian Telecom
context: In September 2016, Jio offered 4G data free for 6 months when rivals charged ₹250/GB. The move was widely called suicidal — instead it forced Vodafone-Idea consolidation, killed Airtel's margins for 3 years, and 5x'd India's data consumption per capita.

title: How Vijay Mallya's Kingfisher Airlines Went From 'King of Good Times' to ₹9,000 Crore Default
context: Mallya's premium-branded airline grew at 30%/year from 2005, then collapsed in 2012 after over-leveraging on the Air Deccan acquisition. Marketing brilliance papered over capital structure cracks.

title: How boAt Built a ₹4,000 Cr Audio Brand Using Cricketers Instead of TV Ads
context: Aman Gupta and Sameer Mehta launched boAt in 2016 by signing micro-priced celebrity endorsements with cricketers and influencers while skipping mainstream advertising. They became India's #1 wearable brand by 2020.

title: Why CRED Spent ₹400 Cr on 'Useless' Celebrity Ads — and Cracked Premium Distribution
context: Kunal Shah's CRED ran intentionally absurd ads featuring Anil Kapoor, Madhuri Dixit and Rahul Dravid that drew mockery in 2021. The strategy was deliberately exclusionary — every user becomes a status signal.

title: How Ramdev's Patanjali Used 'Swadeshi' to Take ₹10,000 Cr from HUL, Nestle, and Colgate
context: From 2012-2017 Patanjali grew from ₹500 Cr to ₹10,000 Cr revenue by positioning multinational brands as foreign exploitation. They cracked rural India through Ayurveda + nationalism.

title: How Nestle Convinced India That a Hot Snack Could Be Made in 2 Minutes
context: Maggi launched in 1983 to a country that had never eaten noodles. The '2-minute' positioning, working-mother ads, and college canteen distribution made it a generation-defining food. The 2015 lead scare nearly killed the brand.

title: How Kodak Invented the Digital Camera in 1975 and Then Killed It Internally
context: Steven Sasson's prototype digital camera was demoed in 1975. Kodak's film-based revenue model led executives to bury the technology for 18 years. They filed for bankruptcy in 2012.

title: When Blockbuster Refused to Buy Netflix for $50 Million — and What Came Next
context: In 2000, Reed Hastings offered to sell Netflix to Blockbuster for $50M. Blockbuster's CEO laughed him out of the room. Blockbuster filed for bankruptcy in 2010; Netflix is now worth $400B+.

title: Elizabeth Holmes and Theranos: How Storytelling Beat Science (Until It Didn't)
context: Theranos raised $9B at peak valuation on the promise of finger-prick blood testing. The technology never worked. The marketing — black turtlenecks, deep voice, photo ops with Kissinger — built a $700M fraud.

title: WeWork's $47B-to-$8B Crash: How a Yoga-Mat IPO Filing Exposed Adam Neumann
context: Neumann took WeWork from a Brooklyn co-working space to a $47B private valuation. The 2019 S-1 revealed lease accounting tricks and ego clauses; valuation collapsed 80% in 6 weeks.

title: Why Deepinder Goyal Bet Zomato on 10-Minute Grocery Delivery When Everyone Said It Was Impossible
context: Zomato acquired Blinkit (formerly Grofers) for $568M in 2022 just as quick-commerce burned cash. By 2024 Blinkit had outgrown Swiggy Instamart and made Zomato profitable on 3x revenue.

title: How Paper Boat Sold ₹100 Aam Panna by Selling Childhood Memories Instead of Juice
context: Hector Beverages launched Paper Boat in 2013 with traditional Indian drinks (aam panna, jaljeera, kokum) at 3x competitor prices. Their marketing was wordless animated nostalgia ads.

title: The Death-Row Confession That Birthed 'Just Do It' — Nike's $43B Three-Word Bet
context: In 1988, agency exec Dan Wieden coined 'Just Do It' inspired by murderer Gary Gilmore's last words ('Let's do it'). Nike's revenue went from $800M (1988) to $9.2B (1998) on the back of that slogan.

title: Why the ₹1 Lakh Tata Nano — Ratan Tata's Dream Car — Failed Spectacularly in India
context: Tata launched the world's cheapest car in 2009 at ₹1 lakh. Positioning it as 'the cheap car for poor families' made it a status anti-symbol. Sales collapsed; production ended 2018.

title: BYJU'S: How India's Most Valuable Startup Wiped Out $22 Billion in 18 Months
context: BYJU'S hit $22B valuation in 2022. Aggressive sales tactics, opaque accounting, and over-acquisition (Aakash, WhiteHat Jr) collapsed it to ~$0 by 2024. A masterclass in growth-at-all-costs.

title: How Ola Outflanked Uber in India by Building for Cash and Hindi-Speaking Drivers
context: When Uber entered India in 2013, Ola was a 100-person startup. Bhavish Aggarwal pivoted to cash payments, Hindi-app interfaces, and tier-2 city expansion. By 2018 Uber India had 40% market share and Ola 60%.

title: How Fevicol Made 'Adhesive' the Most Memorable Ad Category in Indian Television
context: Fevicol's ads — never showing the product, always showing impossible bonds — built Pidilite into a ₹15,000 Cr company. The creative model has stayed unchanged for 30+ years.

title: Why Harley-Davidson Exited India in 2020 After 11 Years and 27,000 Bikes Sold
context: Harley entered India in 2009 expecting premium-bike demand to follow rising incomes. The bikes sold to a tiny weekend-rider niche, dealerships bled cash. They sold the business to Hero MotoCorp.

title: Swiggy Instamart: How Sriharsha Majety Pivoted a Food Delivery App Into Quick Commerce
context: Swiggy launched Instamart in 2020 as a side experiment. By 2024 it contributed 20% of GMV — a moat against Zomato + Zepto. The decision to vertical-integrate dark stores defied the asset-light startup playbook.

title: How MRF Tyres Became Inseparable From Indian Cricket Without Selling a Single Bat
context: MRF has been on Sachin Tendulkar's bat since 1989 — the first major cricket sponsorship in India. The brand spends 0.5% of revenue on advertising and dominates the tyre market with 30%+ share.

title: Yes Bank: How Rana Kapoor Built India's Fastest-Growing Bank Then Personally Destroyed It
context: Yes Bank grew from zero to ₹3.5 lakh crore in 14 years. Kapoor lent aggressively to DHFL, Anil Ambani, Cafe Coffee Day. The bank collapsed in March 2020; SBI led the rescue.

title: How IndiGo Became India's Largest Airline by Refusing to Be Interesting
context: Rahul Bhatia and Rakesh Gangwal launched IndiGo in 2006 with one obsession: 6-minute turnarounds. No frills, one aircraft type, on-time obsession. By 2023 they held 60% domestic market share.

title: Vijay Shekhar Sharma and Paytm: The 8 November 2016 Bet That Made — Then Broke — Him
context: Paytm took out a full-page ad thanking PM Modi on demonetization day. User base went from 125M to 200M in 100 days. The IPO collapsed 75% in 2021; RBI banned Paytm Payments Bank operations in 2024.

title: Naukri.com: How Sanjeev Bikhchandani Built India's Most Profitable Internet Company by Saying No
context: Info Edge (Naukri's parent) has compounded at 30%+ for 25 years by staying boring — no aggressive acquisitions, no overseas adventures, no hype. Made Bikhchandani India's first internet billionaire without burning cash.
